title: AST-extracted API reference
description: API references generated straight from the abstract syntax tree never drift from the code: function signatures, parameters, types, and docstrings are read from source and rendered into docs on every build. Tools like Sphinx autodoc and TypeDoc made this standard — the docs are a view over the code, not a separate artifact.
method: Parse source to AST; extract public symbols with signatures and docstrings; render to HTML/markdown on each build; fail the build on undocumented public symbols if configured.
usage: Write good docstrings (they ARE the docs); run doc generation in CI; treat doc build warnings as errors.

demo.code:
import ast
src = 'def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:\n    """Add two numbers."""\n    return a + b\n'
tree = ast.parse(src)
fn = tree.body[0]
print('extracted:', fn.name, [a.arg for a in fn.args.args], '->', ast.get_docstring(fn))

title: Documentation drift detection
description: Drift detectors compare docs against code and flag mismatches: documented parameters that no longer exist, new parameters nobody documented, examples that no longer run. Running as a CI check, drift detection turns 'docs are outdated' from a complaint into a failing build.
method: Extract documented signature from docs; extract actual signature from code; diff; report missing/extra/changed items as CI failures or warnings.
usage: Run on every PR touching public APIs; start as warnings, graduate to failures once the backlog is clean.

demo.code:
documented, actual = {'a', 'b'}, {'a', 'b', 'c'}
print('drift: undocumented params =', actual - documented, '-> CI warning')

title: Doc-coverage gates
description: Coverage gates measure what fraction of public symbols have documentation and fail the build below a threshold. Like test coverage, the number isn't the point — the gate is: it makes undocumented public API a conscious, visible choice rather than an accident.
method: Count public symbols vs documented ones; compute coverage; fail CI below threshold; track the trend over time.
usage: Set the threshold at your current level, then ratchet it up; exempt internal APIs explicitly.

demo.code:
documented, total = 45, 50
cov = documented / total
print(f'doc coverage {cov:.0%} ->', 'PASS' if cov >= 0.9 else 'FAIL: document 5 more symbols')

title: Architecture decision records (ADRs)
description: ADRs capture why decisions were made, in versioned markdown next to the code. Synchronizers keep the ADR index current and link decisions to the code they affected — when code changes, the linked ADR is flagged for review, so rationale stays attached to reality.
method: One markdown file per decision (context, decision, consequences); index auto-generated; code changes touching decided areas flag linked ADRs for re-review.
usage: Write an ADR for every significant decision; review flagged ADRs when their code changes.

demo.code:
adrs = [{'id': 'ADR-001', 'title': 'Use Postgres', 'areas': ['db/']}] 
print('ADR index:', [(a['id'], a['title']) for a in adrs])
print('change in db/ -> ADR-001 flagged for re-review')

title: Diagram-as-code synchronization
description: Architecture diagrams drawn by hand die with the first refactor. Diagram-as-code (Mermaid, PlantUML, Graphviz) lives in the repo, renders in CI, and can be generated from the code itself (dependency graphs from imports, sequence diagrams from traces) — diagrams that can't drift because they're built from the source of truth.
method: Author diagrams in text; render in CI; optionally generate structural diagrams from code analysis; embed rendered output in docs.
usage: Ban binary diagram files; generate what can be generated; hand-author only what can't.

demo.code:
print('```mermaid')
print('graph LR; A[api] --> B[db]; A --> C[cache]')
print('```')
print('rendered in CI from repo text; dependency graph generated from imports')

title: Doc search index rebuild
description: Documentation is useless if unfindable. The synchronizer rebuilds the full-text search index on every docs deploy — new pages appear in search immediately, renamed pages don't leave ghost results, and the index always matches the published docs exactly.
method: Crawl built docs; extract text per page; build the index (Lunr, Pagefind, Algolia); deploy index with docs atomically.
usage: Rebuild the index in the same pipeline as the docs; never deploy docs without their index.

title: Tutorial testing (executable guides)
description: Tutorials rot faster than API docs because they describe sequences. Executable tutorials run every step as a test — create the project, run the commands, assert the outputs — so a tutorial that no longer works fails CI instead of misleading users.
method: Encode tutorial steps as scripts with assertions; run in a clean container on CI; any step failure marks the tutorial stale.
usage: Keep tutorials' setup hermetic; pin versions; treat tutorial CI as seriously as unit tests.

demo.code:
steps = [('create project', True), ('run build', True), ('assert output', True)]
print('tutorial test:', 'PASS' if all(s[1] for s in steps) else 'STALE')

title: Changelog generation from commits
description: Changelogs written by hand rot; changelogs generated from conventional commits (feat:, fix:, BREAKING CHANGE:) are always complete. Release tooling groups commits by type, links issues, and drafts release notes — the changelog becomes a deterministic function of history.
method: Enforce conventional-commit format; on release, collect commits since last tag; group by type; render markdown; attach to the release.
usage: Lint commit messages in CI; generate the changelog at release time, never by hand.

demo.code:
commits = [('feat', 'add search'), ('fix', 'null crash'), ('feat', 'dark mode')]
from collections import Counter
print('changelog groups:', dict(Counter(t for t, _ in commits)))
